output.summary: A herb native to Europe and southwestern Central Asia, catnip has whitish hairs on its leaves and stems and purple or white, red-speckled flowers. It excites many domestic and large cats. In Roman-era Europe it was valued as tea; its leaves later seasoned meat, sauces and soups.
output.edibilityNote: Historically used as tea in Roman-era Europe; leaves seasoned meat in the Middle Ages and sauces and soups in France.
